sections: The correct sequence in one sentence

Read Boruto: Naruto Next Generations from Chapter 1 through Chapter 80, then begin Boruto: Two Blue Vortex at its Chapter 1 and continue forward. VIZ's official US chapter directories list these as two separately titled parts of the same broader sequel story, with the original series ending at eighty chapters. The numbering resets for the continuation, so a new Chapter 1 does not erase the earlier eighty installments. Readers should finish the first series before starting the second if they want the narrative revelations in order.

The collected editions follow the same structure. Boruto: Naruto Next Generations has twenty English volumes, while Two Blue Vortex begins its own volume sequence with Volume 1. When an online store recommends Boruto Volume 1, check the full title: a book labeled Two Blue Vortex Volume 1 begins much later in the story than the Naruto Next Generations first volume. Matching the series title matters at least as much as matching the number.
Where Naruto itself fits before Boruto

Boruto follows Naruto's son and a new generation of Hidden Leaf shinobi, so the original Naruto manga provides substantial context about the village, older characters and relationships. VIZ's Naruto catalog ends at Chapter 700 and offers the first series as its own reading experience. If you want the complete chronological background, begin with Naruto before moving to Boruto: Naruto Next Generations. That is the most comprehensive approach for someone new to this fictional world.

However, Boruto's opening chapters introduce the young protagonist and his immediate setting, so a reader who already knows the broad Naruto premise can begin directly with Boruto. The essential requirement for avoiding sequel confusion is that Two Blue Vortex is not an introductory manga designed to stand entirely apart from Naruto Next Generations. Readers will encounter major consequences of prior events from its very first volume. Which earlier franchise side stories to read is a matter of interest, not a compulsory numbered prerequisite supplied by VIZ.
Why Chapter 80 is the real dividing line

VIZ's English chapter archive lists Boruto: Naruto Next Generations through Chapter 80. Its Volume 20 product page describes a crucial reversal affecting Boruto and Kawaki, making that final book a natural bridge into the next title. The important transition involves a change in how the protagonists are perceived and a shift in their circumstances. The sequel begins after those developments rather than restoring every relationship to the old status quo.

A spoiler-light guide can identify the break without narrating every detail of the reversal. If you want the surprise to land in the intended order, finish the original chapters instead of opening a summary of Two Blue Vortex first. The edition transition is particularly confusing in digital stores because both series may appear together under a general Boruto brand. The author's name is not sufficient to distinguish them; use the full series title and chapter count.
The reset: Two Blue Vortex Chapter 1 is not a reboot

VIZ's official Two Blue Vortex Volume 1 synopsis presents a Boruto who has been forced away from the Hidden Leaf Village and is training with Sasuke before returning amid new threats. This is continuation after a major shift, not a separate retelling of the first academy chapters. The new title and chapter numbering make it accessible as a publishing unit, but they do not erase the causes of its characters' circumstances.

Starting from the newer book's Chapter 1 is correct only after that transition. Online comments sometimes call it Boruto Part 2; that is useful casual shorthand for the manga, but should not be confused with the separate Boruto anime Part 2 production announcement. The formats and the production schedules are independently maintained.
Volumes and individual chapters are different products

A collected paperback groups chapters that previously appeared in serialization; an online chapter listing gives access to individual installments on a different release cycle. VIZ lists the US English Naruto Next Generations Volume 20 as a 216-page paperback released August 6, 2024. Two Blue Vortex Volume 1, by contrast, is a separate 184-page paperback released February 4, 2025. Those dates are publication records for the books, not the original online debut dates of every chapter inside them.

Readers building a shelf should follow the numbered volumes within each of the two series, while digital readers can follow the published chapter indexes. A bookstore may show the newest imported Japanese volume before its English edition is released; that does not mean the English publisher is missing chapters without explanation. Make sure the language, format and ISBN correspond to your actual buying goal.
Where US readers can read legally in English

VIZ publishes official English Shonen Jump chapter pages for both Boruto series. Its directories also direct readers to MANGA Plus by Shueisha for certain free chapters, while additional chapters may require joining the service. Access conditions can vary by episode or account and change over time. The presence of several free introductory chapters does not guarantee the entire archive can be read for free forever or downloaded as files.

To follow the story, open the official Naruto Next Generations chapter directory and finish through Chapter 80 using whatever licensed access applies to your account. Then navigate to the separate Two Blue Vortex index and begin with its Chapter 1. If you prefer purchasing books, choose the VIZ volume listings under the correct title. Avoid reading on an unlicensed mirror when the legitimate publisher provides a clear sequence.
Manga and anime numbers should not be interchanged

The Boruto: Naruto Next Generations anime ran to Episode 293 before Part 1 ended in 2023. That episode number is not a reference to manga Chapter 293. Television adaptations can add original storylines, rearrange events or divide arcs in ways that do not match the manga's collected edition boundaries. A viewer trying to continue directly from the anime should establish what story has actually been adapted before selecting an exact manga handoff point.

This guide deliberately does not manufacture a universal episode-to-chapter conversion. The safe manga reading order is clear independently of the television adaptation, and the future anime's release date remains a separate unresolved question. Readers who want to avoid missing character development can start with the earliest manga chapters rather than rely on a guessed point derived from episode numbering.
How to check that you're on the right page

A reliable chapter page should display both the title and the installment number. The original listing reads Boruto: Naruto Next Generations, while the continuation reads Boruto: Two Blue Vortex. The first ends at Chapter 80; the second begins at Chapter 1, and its newer chapter entries continue to appear independently. A third-party app might abbreviate these labels to Boruto, which makes a verified VIZ URL a useful reference.

The one-line answer for a US reader is original twenty-volume Boruto series first, then Two Blue Vortex from its own first volume or chapter. This approach keeps the timeline, the numbering reset and the purchase model distinct. The guide should be revised only if the publisher changes its access terms or issues a meaningful edition correction, not to artificially refresh its modified date every month.

sections: The current official credit line settles the central question

VIZ's current English Two Blue Vortex chapter directory credits Masashi Kishimoto with creation and supervision, and Mikio Ikemoto with artwork. Those are the most dependable public labels for the continuing manga as of November 15, 2026. A reader trying to identify the person drawing Boruto's current appearances should look to Ikemoto, not to Kishimoto's direct drawing work on the original Naruto manga. The source does not list the same person in both roles.

That distinction is often lost in social media shorthand. Calling a comic Kishimoto's Boruto may refer to his original world and supervisory role, while claiming Kishimoto personally draws every Two Blue Vortex chapter is a different and unsupported statement. A publisher's credit line is more useful than assumptions formed from which artist's style a reader prefers. The question is not which name is more famous; it is what the authorized edition actually attributes to each contributor.
Kishimoto created Naruto before supervising Boruto

Masashi Kishimoto wrote and drew the original Naruto manga, establishing its central characters and world long before the sequel began. His position in Boruto is therefore rooted in authorship of the franchise itself. VIZ uses the phrasing creation or supervision on the sequel's present listings. That is a role related to overall story direction and creative oversight, rather than an automatically comprehensive statement about who draws panels or pens each line of dialogue.

Credits describe an approved collaborative structure but may not expose the private workflow of draft revisions, editorial meetings or assistants. It would be misleading to infer that Kishimoto personally writes every speech balloon on a particular page merely from the words creation or supervision. Conversely, it would also be inaccurate to claim he has no creative involvement because another artist is publicly credited. The reliable answer preserves the distinctions the publisher chose.
Ikemoto is the ongoing Boruto manga artist

Mikio Ikemoto is credited by VIZ as the artist for both Boruto: Naruto Next Generations and Boruto: Two Blue Vortex. His work supplies the sequel's visual identity, from the main characters' designs to page layouts and action illustration. The published volume listings maintain this attribution across the first and second manga titles. A separate Shadow Rising project drawn by Kishimoto does not transfer Boruto's art responsibilities to him by implication.

Readers can reasonably compare Ikemoto's style with Kishimoto's original Naruto work as a matter of criticism. However, the existence of those stylistic differences is not evidence of an unannounced artist replacement. A good analysis should discuss composition and character design with examples from authorized pages, rather than pretend that an artist's visibility determines whether his contributions deserve credit. The two manga have related worlds but distinct artistic production.
Ukyo Kodachi's early script contribution matters

The original Boruto manga was initially associated with a team that included scriptwriter Ukyo Kodachi. VIZ's legacy listing explicitly carries the script credit, alongside Kishimoto's creation or supervision and Ikemoto's art. It is therefore inaccurate to erase Kodachi from the early manga history or to apply present-day credits backward as though no change ever occurred. Early Boruto chapters and later Two Blue Vortex issues should be contextualized within their respective production periods.

This is particularly relevant when readers compare the storytelling before and after a major transition. A change in script responsibility may influence tone or structure, but claims of direct causation need supporting evidence and close reading. One cannot assert that every creative decision was made by a single person just because the public credit arrangement changed. The first step is to identify accurately who is named in the editions and when.
The 2020 announcement changed the story-writing arrangement

Contemporaneous reporting of the franchise's November 2020 communication says the Boruto manga production system would change around Chapter 52, with Kishimoto's original drafts becoming the basis for the continuing story. Kodachi's tenure in the script role was recognized as the series moved into this arrangement. That historical record is important because it explains why older product pages may include Kodachi while current Two Blue Vortex entries center Kishimoto and Ikemoto.

Some English headlines summarized the development as Kishimoto taking over writing. That captures the direction of the announced change but should not be turned into a detailed account of unseen manuscript workflows. The Japanese statement's references to original drafts and planned production changes establish a shift, not a public breakdown of every contributor's daily tasks. VIZ's present role labels remain the most straightforward reference for a current American chapter.
Two Blue Vortex is the continuation, not a second artist's reboot

Boruto: Two Blue Vortex begins with a new title and chapter sequence after Naruto Next Generations ended at Chapter 80. The shift includes a change in the characters' circumstances and timeline, but VIZ still credits Ikemoto for the art and Kishimoto for creation or supervision. The new title should not be treated as proof that the original Naruto artist took over the drawing or that Kodachi returned to script it without a stated credit.

The publication's changing story period can generate new character designs and a distinct atmosphere, which are normal consequences of a serialized continuation. Those are appropriate topics for art criticism. Accurate creator attribution is the prerequisite: a guide that calls every changed design Kishimoto's drawing risks taking credit away from the artist actually identified on the book.
What this means for Kishimoto's Shadow Rising manga

At New York Comic Con in October 2026, the Naruto rights holders also announced a new manga drawn directly by Kishimoto, named Naruto: Shadow Rising in the Japanese official communication. That is noteworthy precisely because the project advertises the original author's personal drawing work, whereas VIZ's Two Blue Vortex credits identify Ikemoto as the ongoing artist. They are concurrent creative announcements, not interchangeable labels.

There is no evidence in those statements that Kishimoto's drawing a new Naruto work cancels Boruto: Two Blue Vortex or forces Ikemoto off its art team. Nor is the Shadow Rising publication length publicly defined, so assumptions about its effect on the wider production are speculative. Fans should follow the separate official series listings as more information appears, instead of using one teaser to infer another book's unannounced staffing.
A practical credit-checking method for readers

When a new manga announcement circulates, open the authorized chapter directory or product page and look for the specific labels attached to each contributor: story, script, creation, supervision, artwork or illustration. Then note the date or volume of the edition. Credits can change over a long serial, and an early-series page may preserve names that do not appear in the current continuation. This method is more reliable than a social media post referring generically to the Naruto author.

The concise answer is that Kishimoto remains the original creator and listed supervisor, Ikemoto draws Two Blue Vortex, and Kodachi holds an important historical early script credit on Naruto Next Generations. The November 2020 transition helps explain the change in wording. Those distinctions offer useful context for a fair analysis of the story and art while acknowledging that private editorial workflows are not fully visible from public listings.

What qualifies as an important announcement after the stage

For Shadow Rising, the high-value news would be an exact first-chapter publication date, format, magazine and official English reading arrangements. For Naruto × Ninkū, it would be a broadcast day, channel and US streaming rights. For the Naruto Card Game, a product catalog and regional retail information would be useful. For Naruto Mobile, supported countries and devices would turn a broad promise into an actionable US guide. Every future piece should be anchored to a dated primary statement.

The event itself is already confirmed: December 19–20, 2026, with Naruto's Saturday 16:55–17:25 JST presentation. This article should be updated after the actual stage rather than pretending in November to know its surprises. Its editorial value is to give US fans a trustworthy watchlist of questions while keeping the original manga, anime, games and live-action movie announcements separate.

sections: What is actually confirmed about Boruto Chapter 39?

Boruto: Two Blue Vortex Chapter 39 has not been published at the time of this preview, November 15, 2026. The Naruto and Boruto official website announced on November 13 that the new chapter will appear in the January 2027 super-sized issue of V Jump, on sale in Japan on Friday, November 20, 2026, Japan Standard Time. The issue's cover month is not the same as its real-world sale month. In other words, the January edition arrives in November. The official post also shows one preview page, but it does not disclose the full chapter's title, ending or the resolution of the ongoing battles.

VIZ's official English Two Blue Vortex listing still identifies Chapter 38, dated October 20, as the latest released installment as of this research check. Its listing says a new chapter is coming shortly. Readers in the United States may see the digital chapter on November 19 because the services display their own local publication times; the authoritative date currently confirmed by the Japanese publisher is November 20 in Japan. Check VIZ or Shueisha's MANGA Plus directly for the precise English release countdown in your region. Any article that treats a fan-posted scan or an early translated excerpt as the final official English chapter before publication is getting ahead of the evidence.

This is a preview, not a review. It separates three categories that should not be blurred: confirmed facts from publisher announcements, established events in the already-released Chapter 38, and predictions made before Chapter 39 is available. There is no claim that the full new chapter has been read, no invented chapter title, no verdict on its quality and no numerical rating. A full post-release review should be written from the actual published installment rather than converted from guesses that happen to resemble some of its events.
What the official preview shows: Kawaki and Himawari at home

The first officially released Chapter 39 preview draws attention away from the cliffhanger at the Divine Trees' hideout. Reporting on the page describes Kawaki sitting down to eat curry made by Himawari in the Uzumaki home. The conversation centers on cooking. Himawari explains that she did not need to add water because moisture from the ingredients was sufficient, and Kawaki reacts with surprise. It is an ordinary family scene, not a newly confirmed fight or supernatural revelation. The distinction matters because the preview communicates a mood rather than an entire plot direction.

That small exchange becomes more significant when set against the family's history. Kawaki has confined Naruto and Hinata in Daikokuten and continues to treat Boruto as someone he may have to kill. Omnipotence changed how most people remember Boruto and Kawaki's places in the Uzumaki household. Kawaki can occupy a domestic role that Boruto has been forced away from even while maintaining a dangerous secret about the parents whose home it is. Sharing a meal therefore creates an uncomfortable contrast between the warmth of an ordinary kitchen and the decisions that have made the household incomplete.

An important correction to simplistic fan claims comes from Mikio Ikemoto's official Q&A on the Naruto site. The creator explains that Himawari chose to live in the Uzumaki house because she hopes her parents will return and wants it to remain a home for them. He also says that, after Omnipotence, Himawari was worried about Boruto and sought Sarada's advice. That evidence does not support the claim that she has forgotten every feeling for her actual brother or consciously accepted every aspect of Kawaki's story. The domestic scene can be read as her trying to maintain family bonds while living with incomplete information. Whether it leads to new suspicions or only provides an emotional pause is not yet confirmed.
The strongest prediction: Kawaki's quiet evening may expose a contradiction

The official sneak peek makes a conversation between Himawari and Kawaki the clearest available lead. One possible development is that a casual exchange reveals some inconsistency between Kawaki's personality and the memories people have of the Hokage's son. Fans discussing the preview on Reddit have speculated that Himawari may notice responses that do not match what she remembers. This is a reasonable question for the manga to explore because Omnipotence did not make all characters indifferent to contradictions; it made the remembered history extraordinarily difficult to challenge.

But there is an equally plausible, less dramatic possibility. The conversation may establish that Kawaki wants to behave like a family member and that Himawari is willing to offer kindness without understanding or endorsing his actions. His past includes deprivation and manipulation, and ordinary meals with Naruto's family were one of the first experiences of safety he received. The preview might be less about a sudden breakdown of the memory effect than about a person briefly returning to the domestic life he is simultaneously destroying. Such an interlude would fit the chapter's wider interest in how powerful people justify harm while insisting they care about someone.

Neither scenario should be presented as a confirmed reveal. The released preview does not show Himawari recognizing a full identity swap, Kawaki confessing that Naruto and Hinata are sealed, or the siblings agreeing about Boruto's innocence. Those would be major story developments, and there is no verified basis for announcing them on the strength of a meal and a few translated speech bubbles. A prediction is most useful when it identifies the choice the author has placed under pressure, not when it invents an ending.
Boruto versus Code: confrontation is expected, victory is not guaranteed

Chapter 38 ended with Boruto reaching Sarada after she improvised a chakra trace when Code removed the prepared teleportation markers. Boruto attacked Code at the hideout, interrupting an immediate threat to her. This is the most direct action thread that Chapter 39 could resume. Code has wanted Boruto to confront him for a long time, and his original effort to use Sarada as leverage has failed in the most humiliating way: his supposed hostage was able to make the protagonist arrive despite his precautions. A renewed exchange of attacks is a sensible expectation based on where the previous installment stopped.

Yet the narrative objective is not necessarily Code's defeat. Boruto is entering the territory of the Divine Trees with Sarada injured and Hidari present. Even if he possesses the strength to damage Code, choosing to chase the villain could leave Sarada exposed or bring Jura into a fight at an unfavorable time. A more interesting prediction is that Boruto will prioritize removing her from immediate danger while Code struggles to reestablish his original plan. Code could retreat through a Claw Mark, attack from an unexpected direction or attempt to redirect the other creatures against Boruto. None of those outcomes has been confirmed by the available preview.

Readers should also resist the assumption that a single spectacular entrance makes a character's power ranking final. The purpose of the Chapter 38 ending was to change a failing rescue into a new, dangerous confrontation. The next chapter may test Boruto's judgment more severely than his raw strength. A protagonist who has already risked his body through a bargain with Momoshiki has good reason to keep the rescue short. A prolonged fight could accomplish everything Code wants while advancing the very future Koji is trying to prevent.
Hidari could change the fight for reasons nobody understands yet

Hidari's behavior creates an unpredictable third interest in the hideout. He is connected to Sasuke, wants Sarada for his own reasons and has shown an unwillingness to allow Code to harm her in particular ways. In Chapter 38, that contradiction disrupted Code's control of the encounter. It would make sense for the manga to develop the conflict between an antagonist who views Sarada as bait and a sentient Divine Tree who treats her as the focus of a separate instinct. A temporary clash between Code and Hidari could create a route for Boruto and Sarada to escape.

A more speculative possibility is that some part of Sasuke's parental protectiveness is influencing Hidari. The story has repeatedly asked whether the evolved Divine Trees inherit emotional tendencies from the people whose chakra and circumstances produced them. Jura's attachment to Hidari has given that question fresh urgency. Even so, one intervention does not prove that Hidari is secretly controlled by Sasuke or that his interest in Sarada is benevolent. He may want to preserve her only because he intends to consume her himself. Both readings remain possible; the chapter must show more evidence before either can be treated as an answer.

Reddit discussions have also suggested that Jura could interrupt the encounter if Hidari is endangered. That forecast has a narrative basis because Jura has admitted that losing Hidari matters to him. But an interruption is not inevitable. Jura is occupied by an ordinary bookshop visit arranged to delay his return to the hideout. The story may deliberately use that separation to give Sarada and Boruto a narrow window. The possibilities are best understood as competing tensions, not spoilers.
Momoshiki remains the danger inside Boruto's rescue

Kashin Koji has warned that a future involving Sarada's rescue may increase the danger of Momoshiki taking over Boruto. This is not the same as saying the takeover has already occurred or that it will certainly happen on the first page of Chapter 39. Koji's Prescience concerns possible outcomes affected by decisions in the present, and earlier chapters demonstrated that acting on a prediction can change the conditions that produced it. Boruto nevertheless knows that Momoshiki has been waiting for an opportunity to benefit from his emotional distress and from the bargain that made Karma useful again.

The hideout confrontation provides several plausible triggers for a loss of control: Boruto might become desperate if Sarada is badly hurt, use Karma beyond what the agreement safely permits, or discover that his own intentions and Momoshiki's are no longer aligned. These are scenarios built from the preceding chapter, not verified events from the new one. The more compelling question is whether Boruto can protect Sarada without treating his own future autonomy as something he may spend freely. He has a tendency to assume the cost of a plan should fall on him alone, but a hostile takeover would affect many people beyond himself.

Official creator commentary has distinguished Momoshiki's ability to glimpse fragments of the future from Koji's more powerful Prescience. That distinction is relevant because both parties may possess incomplete information. A character who sees a possible disaster can still be mistaken about the exact route to it. Chapter 39 could emphasize that uncertainty rather than simply deliver a predetermined possession scene. It would also help preserve the significance of Boruto's own choices when an unusual number of people in the story can foresee some version of what he might do.
Shikamaru's political problem might become the real turning point

While the rescue occupies the center of the action, Konoha's leadership is under pressure. Kobu possesses material that appears to implicate Shikamaru in Boruto's escape. The acting Hokage cannot easily explain why he worked with the person the village remembers as Naruto's murderer, because the official history itself is compromised by Omnipotence. The investigator's agenda also extends beyond punishing a single official: the possibility of reducing the influence of ninja villages has been raised, and Konohamaru is discussed as someone who could be elevated while real control shifts elsewhere.

The story has not confirmed Konohamaru as the Ninth Hokage. That needs to remain clear in any preview. Kobu can want a change, possess evidence and move toward a political showdown without having already achieved the appointment. Chapter 39 might show Shikamaru questioning the documents, negotiating for more time, confronting the investigator or beginning to lose the authority he needs to coordinate the defense. Alternatively, the chapter may leave the political arc in place while focusing on the hideout and the domestic preview. Nothing from the official Chapter 39 excerpt resolves the issue.

What makes this possibility interesting is that Boruto's public situation can worsen even if he wins a fight. Losing a competent insider could sever his route to Konoha's defenses and leave the village unable to interpret warnings from Koji. The external pressure against the ninja system also asks a legitimate political question: are institutions created for armed villages still capable of governing a world increasingly shaped by science and cosmic-scale threats? The story is strongest when that debate remains substantive rather than making every skeptical official a cartoon villain.
What fans are discussing—and what no leak has proved

The discussion around the preview shows several different expectations rather than a single settled theory. In a publicly accessible November 13 Reddit discussion of the Kawaki and Himawari page, some fans read the meal as new symbolism for Kawaki's place in the Uzumaki family, while others wondered whether Himawari might notice inconsistencies in his behavior. A separate r/Boruto predictions discussion before release raises ideas about Code escaping to warn Jura, Hidari speaking to Sarada rather than immediately fighting her, or the political conflict between Shikamaru and Kobu continuing. These are examples of fan interpretation, not reporting from the publisher.

It is useful to compare such ideas with the few facts the publisher has made public. The release date is announced. One preview page has been published. Chapter 38 is available in the English directory. The larger plots involving Boruto, Sarada, Code, Hidari, Momoshiki and Konoha's government remain unresolved. No verified official Chapter 39 title, complete ending or final battle result was available in the sources checked for this article. A screenshot posted by a fan, particularly one using an unofficial translation, is not sufficient to overturn those boundaries.

This matters for the quality of anime and manga coverage. Prediction articles often turn a plausible development into a declaration that a character has died, betrayed somebody or acquired a new power. When the official chapter finally appears, readers are left trying to separate genuine story events from predictions recycled as spoilers. Our approach is to state why an outcome would make narrative sense while leaving room for the writer to do something else. A correct guess is not the same as an advance source of facts.
What we will look for when the full chapter arrives

After the official English release, the review should begin with what the finished installment actually does rather than whether our predictions were accurate. Did the Kawaki and Himawari scene deepen a complicated relationship, or merely delay the central fight? Did Sarada contribute to the resolution after creating the route Boruto used to find her? Did Code behave like a dangerous adversary despite his recent failures? Did Hidari show evidence of an independent protective instinct, and did the writing preserve the consequences for Sasuke? Each of these questions tests a specific part of the chapter's storytelling.

The review should also examine the limits of Koji's warning. A successful rescue and a failed possession prediction would not automatically mean his powers are useless; future probabilities can change as people act. Conversely, a sudden Momoshiki takeover should not be praised as a twist merely because it was predicted. Its emotional and causal consequences would need to be coherent. Shikamaru's political crisis deserves the same care: the installment's quality should depend on how intelligently it handles trust, accountability and altered memory, not simply on whether an important official is removed.

This pre-release page will remain a dated record of what was knowable on November 15. It should not later be rewritten to pretend the prediction sections were facts. Once the manga releases, a distinct Chapter 39 review can assess the actual published story with its official title, substantive criticism, sourced observations and a fresh update date. Until then the safest reading route is to finish Chapter 38 through VIZ or MANGA Plus, view the publisher's preview and treat every proposed Chapter 39 outcome as a possibility rather than a promised event.
